$comment: Phase 5. A SECOND axis space, composed sequentially with the belief axes, not added to them.
beliefs (17 axes)  ->  which agendas and policy levers are worth your time
culture (9 axes)   ->  where you would do that work well
Ids are prefixed `c_` and must never collide with a belief axis id. verify asserts that the two
spaces do not leak into each other in either direction.
POLICY, NOT A GAP: organizations do not get belief coordinates. Not now, not later. Beliefs
belong to agendas and to individuals; culture belongs to organizations. Where an org's belief
position is genuinely needed, only the house-view cross-term in the ranking, its primary
agenda's coordinates stand in, which is the honest claim: an org's belief position is inherited
from the work it does. verify asserts no org carries a non-null belief coordinate, so a later
pass cannot 'fix' this by populating them.
Stability is deliberately NOT a tenth axis. It is already on orgs.csv as `maturity_tier`, and
duplicating it as a scored dimension would double-count it in the distance metric.
Sequential composition. Beliefs decide WHAT; culture reranks WHERE, within the role set the
beliefs already produced. Culture never adds a role, never removes one, and never reorders
agendas, a joint metric would let strong culture fit pull someone toward an agenda they
think is doomed, which is backwards.
The one legitimate cross-term is `kappa`. Joining an org with a strong shared position is a
worse fit if you disagree with that position; at a pluralistic org the same distance matters
much less. The penalty is displayed as a named reason, never as an unexplained rank drop.
